### 11.5 Easy Caulimash (Keto "Mashed Potatoes")

Transcribed from a printed keto cookbook page (p. 210) — the same book as [§11.4 Southern Fauxtato Salad](114-southern-fauxtato-salad-cauliflower-potato-salad.md), and the same swap: **cauliflower standing in for potatoes**. This fills what was the *Southern Keto Mashed Potatoes* placeholder.

**Yield:** 4 servings *(the printed recipe; the house blend in B2 is roughly four times this — see that section)*

**🥑 Keto** · **🟢 Easy** · **Prep ~5 min** · **Cook ~10 min** · **Start to finish ~15 min**

**⏰ Countdown to dinner:** T−15 min cook the cauliflower per the package, drain well · T−5 min into the processor with the butter and cream, pulse smooth, season · T−0 serve, more butter if you like. *(The house blend in B2 runs longer — about T−45 min to break down and boil 2 fresh heads and 4 potatoes, T−10 min to blend and fold.)*

**❤️ Family favorite** — *Cody: "Wonderful."*

> **The one step not to skip: drain it properly.** Frozen cauliflower carries a lot of water, and the source is blunt about it — *"you don't want watery caulimash."* Drain the excess liquid before it goes in the processor or the texture never comes together.

#### A. Ingredients

- 1 (12 oz.) bag frozen cauliflower florets
- 3 Tbsp salted butter, plus extra for garnish if desired
- 2 Tbsp heavy whipping cream
- Salt and ground black pepper

#### B. Cooking Instructions

**1. Cook the cauliflower per the package, then drain well.**
Drain off the excess liquid thoroughly — see the note above; this is the step that decides whether you get mash or soup.

**2. Blend with the butter and cream until smooth and creamy.**
Cauliflower into a food processor or high-powered blender, add the butter and cream, and pulse until smooth. Season to taste with salt and pepper. *A processor or high-powered blender isn't strictly required, but it makes a real difference to the texture — an immersion blender in the pot also works.*

**3. Serve, garnished with more butter if you like.**

#### B2. Variation — The Cauliflower-and-Potato Blend (the house version, tested — and it is not keto)

✅ **The idea is his wife's, 2026-09-09: *"My wife likes to mix just a couple of mashed potatoes in there — maybe twenty percent mashed potatoes. Refine that recipe."*** The potato brings back the starch and the body that cauliflower alone never quite has, so the bowl reads as mashed potatoes with a lighter texture rather than as cauliflower with something in it.

✅ **And they cooked it — Cody, 2026-09-13, with the real quantities: *"We actually got two heads of fresh cauliflower, and then we mixed it with two medium-to-small potatoes per head of cauliflower. So I guess there was four total, and that seems to be a really good compromise for the cauliflower mash."*** **These are his figures and they supersede the cookbook's earlier estimate** — the *"about ½ cup, roughly 20%"* written here on 2026-09-09 was judgment, and it was low. His tested ratio is **two medium-to-small potatoes for every head of cauliflower**, which by weight lands nearer a quarter to a third potato than a fifth. *(Rough arithmetic, the cookbook's: a medium head trims to something like 1½ lb of florets, and a medium-to-small potato runs 4 to 6 oz, so four potatoes against two heads is roughly 1 to 1½ lb of potato against 3 lb of cauliflower. The number that matters is his — two per head — not the percentage.)*

**Two other things change with his version, and they are worth saying plainly:** it is **fresh cauliflower, not the source's frozen bag**, and **two heads is a much bigger batch** than the printed recipe — roughly four times it. The printed recipe in Section A above is untouched; this is the family-sized way they actually make it.

**1. Break down 2 heads of fresh cauliflower and cook them until fully tender.** Core them and cut into florets; steam or boil until a fork goes through with no resistance — undercooked cauliflower never mashes smooth, it just goes grainy. **Then drain it hard**, and give it a minute in the hot dry pot to steam off. The drain warning at the top of this entry matters more with fresh than with frozen, because you are cooking it in water rather than heating it from a bag.

**2. At the same time, peel and boil 4 medium-to-small potatoes — two per head of cauliflower — and mash them.** His ratio. Cut them to an even size so they finish together, boil until a knife slides out clean, drain, and mash while hot. *([§5.25 Heather's Mashed Potatoes](525-heathers-mashed-potatoes.md) ❤️ is the house mashed potato if you want them made that way; plain boiled-and-mashed is what this blend needs.)*

**3. Blend the cauliflower smooth with butter and cream, then fold the potatoes in by hand.** Cauliflower into the processor with the butter and cream and pulse smooth, as in Step 2 of the main recipe; **then fold the warm mashed potato in with a spoon, off the machine.** Warm potatoes fold in cleanly and cold ones go lumpy — and **over-worked potato turns gluey**, which is the one way to ruin this. Taste for salt at the end, since the potatoes carry their own.

*⚙️ **Scaling the butter and cream is the cookbook's arithmetic, not his** — he gave the vegetables, not the dairy. Four times the printed batch is roughly **¾ cup of butter and ½ cup of cream**, added to taste rather than measured in; the potatoes will want a little of their own. His own figures replace these the day he gives them.*

> 🥑 **This variation is not keto, and the entry's tag does not extend to it — and at his tested ratio it is further from keto than the earlier estimate suggested.** The plain recipe prints **4.9 g net carbs per serving**. Four medium-to-small potatoes carry on the order of **25 to 30 g of carbohydrate each once you account for size**, so the blend adds something like **100 g of carbohydrate across the whole batch**. Spread over the batch's own larger yield that lands in the neighborhood of **8 to 12 g of net carbs a serving** — two to three times the printed figure. That is a rough cookbook estimate per [CLAUDE.md §3b](../../CLAUDE.md), built on USDA-scale figures rather than any printed number, and it moves with potato size and what goes in them. **The point is the direction, not the decimal: this is a lighter mashed potato, not a keto side.** The ❤️ and the 🟢 are unchanged — it's the same ten minutes with one more bowl.

#### C. Grocery Shopping List

**🛒 General grocery**

- 🛒 Frozen cauliflower florets — 1 × 12 oz. bag
- 🛒 **Fresh cauliflower — 2 heads**, *only for the house blend (B2)*; the printed recipe above uses the frozen bag instead
- 🛒 **Potatoes — 4 medium-to-small**, *only for the house blend (B2)* — two per head of cauliflower, Cody's ratio
- 🛒 Salted butter — 3 Tbsp, plus extra for garnish
- 🛒 Heavy whipping cream — 2 Tbsp
- 🛒 Salt and ground black pepper

**Not a grocery item, but worth having:** a food processor, high-powered blender, or immersion blender.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
